articles.title: Mayer vs Cameron: Caroline Dubois eyes Alycia Baumgardner and Elif Nur Turhan fights after Ameila Moore clash
articles.summary: Caroline Dubois will take on Amelia Moore in Birmingham on August 29; the event will be headlined by Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron, who will compete for the unified welterweight world championship; watch MVPW-06 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Dubois will seek to maintain her unbeaten record when she defends her WBC and WBO straps against Moore at MVPW-06 at the bp pulse LIVE, live on Sky Sports, in their bout on the undercard of Chantelle Cameron's clash with Mikaela Mayer.

While the British boxer asserts she is chomping at the bit for her upcoming fight, she is not shy about using her platform to share her loftier ambitions to unify the world lightweight division.

"To be honest, I always think about what's next," Dubois told Sky Sports .

"Not to be distracted about what is in front of me, but I believe in setting goals. I believe in setting little goals, big goals, massive goals and having timelines.

"For me, the biggest timeline has to be becoming undisputed. We have two more champions in the weight division, [Stephanie] Han and [Elif Nur] Turhan. Whichever one makes the most sense, whichever one is more feasible and accessible for the next fight, we have to go after that.

"It's not about announcing myself - I've already been announced - but cementing myself as the world champion and proving to the world why I'm the world champion, why I'm the only unified world champion.

"It's about sending a message to the rest of the 135ers [in Dubois' weight division] that the queen is in town and this is what's up - I'm coming for the belts!"

Dubois and Moore shared an icy stare down as the pair faced off on Tuesday, the latter insisting she is unshakeable while her champion London rival suggested she has seen nothing in Moore that could trouble her.

"These are my belts, I've worked very hard for them and Amelia Moore isn't going to do anything to take them from me," said Dubois.

"She was around for three Olympic cycles and I qualified first time. I've seen her coming up in the amateurs. I remember going to Colorado and doing an international training camp and she was there.

"I knew about her from the amateurs, she turned professional of course, she slipped off the radar and now she's back so we'll see.

"This is my time to shine, there's no pressure, just excitement. I can't wait to go out there and perform and have fun, there's no expectations."

'I want to punch her in the face and get this over with'

Dubois has no problem expressing her desire to achieve her long-term targets, but her focus remains firmly on putting in a dominant performance against Moore in Birmingham.

"I just can't wait to step into the ring, punch her in the face and get this over with," she said.

"We're going to see vintage Caroline Dubois and we're going to see complete domination.

"I'm not going to focus too much on getting the stoppage. I'm just going to focus on going out there and having fun.

"I just know I'm going to go out there and do my thing, which is going to be look very good and look very exciting. Body, head, attacks, aggressive - vintage."

Dubois: Baumgardner is playing it safe by not fighting me

The Brit was thrilled to learn that unified junior lightweight champion Alycia Baumgardner - who previously insisted that Dubois still needs to prove herself before earning a fight against her - was set to be ringside for the fight against Moore.

"I didn't know that. Is that true? I need to see her - this is great," Dubois told Sky Sports .

"I'm going to go to the gym with a smile on my face. I'm very excited - I can't wait! This is going to be great.

"Boxing is about rivalries, it's about clashes. At the end of the day, boxing is about two people believing what they're better than each other and clashing. It's very rare, unfortunately, with female boxing where you have a fighter who's confident enough to say that.

"With myself and Alycia, I think we're the only two girls right now, besides Claressa Shields, who's confident enough to say: 'I believe I'm going to take your head off your shoulders and I believe I'm the best in the division.'"

Dubois, though, did not change her critical stance on Baumgardner, who she called "lost" for not agreeing to fight her , and is still targeting a shot at the American.

"Alycia likes to play it safe. She's been beaten already.

"Once you lose in professional boxing, unfortunately, people can be very cutthroat and forget all you did to get there. She's already experienced that and now she wants to play everything safe.

"She wanted to fight Amanda Serrano. She wanted to fight Katie Taylor. She wanted to fight all these women who are retiring and are at the end of their careers. She did not want to go after the big dogs because she knows how dangerous it can be.

"I just want to fight the best. I have no issues - I believe in myself and I back myself, I just want it.

"For me, all I care about is being involved in the biggest fights, the most exciting fights. I just see Alycia as being such an exciting fight for myself."

Baumgardner will move up a division to fight Elif Nur Turhan for her IBF lightweight world title on November 8 - live on Sky Sports - in a seismic move that brings a blockbuster showdown with Dubois a step closer.

articles.title: Alycia Baumgardner to step up to Caroline Dubois' division and fight Elif Nur Turhan for IBF world title
articles.summary: Alycia Baumgardner will challenge IBF lightweight champion Elif Nur Turhan on November 8 in a bid to become a two-weight world champion; victory would move unified super featherweight champion closer to a blockbuster unification showdown with WBC and WBO champion Caroline Dubois
articles.body:
Baumgardner, the reigning unified WBO, WBA and IBF super featherweight world champion, will jump up five pounds to the 135lbs division to face the undefeated Turhan in the headline bout of MVPW-07 at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas.

"When I set my mind to something, I see it through, and 135 will be no different," Baumgardner said. "This is a super fight, the kind of fight boxing deserves, and the beginning of my next chapter.

"I know what it takes to become undisputed. I've done it before, and I'll do it again."

Turhan added: "Alycia is a boxer who steps into the ring determined to win, never even entertaining the possibility of defeat. I know I am facing an opponent who steps into the ring solely for victory.

"I do not want to lose either. As two boxers sharing a 'win at all costs' mentality, we guarantee a fierce, relentless battle where everything is left on the line. Two warriors, one fight and only one winner."

Victory for Baumgardner would see her become a two-weight world champion in the same division as Dubois, who holds the WBC and WBO titles.

The 32-year-old is set to be ringside for Dubois' clash with Amelia Moore on Saturday, live on Sky Sports .

Since December, Dubois has been vociferous in calling out Baumgardner, and those calls have only intensified since she beat Terri Harper to unify the division in April.

Baumgardner has maintained that, despite her status as a unified world champion, Dubois has yet to reach the level required for her to entertain a fight between them.

But should Baumgardner inflict a first career defeat on Turhan, all roads will surely lead to a blockbuster unification bout with Dubois, where the winner would move to within one victory of becoming undisputed champion.

The co-main event on November 8 will see England's Ellie Scotney fight the undefeated Tiara Brown over 10 rounds for the WBC featherweight world title.

Former undisputed super bantamweight champion Scotney will step up to 126lbs as she bids to become a two-weight world champion.

"MVPW-07 is one of the biggest championship events in boxing history, with four back-to-back world title fights, bringing together eight elite fighters from around the world with belts at stake in every match-up," said Nakisa Bidarian and Jake Paul, co-founders of Most Valuable Promotions.

articles.title: UFC Shanghai: Yan Xiaonan puts title talk aside ahead of Denise Gomes fight
articles.summary: MMA News: Yan Xiaonan has spent more than a year away from the UFC. She returns on Saturday in Shanghai as the No. 4-ranked women's strawweight, taking on No. 1.
articles.body: Yan Xiaonan has spent more than a year away from the UFC. She returns on Saturday in Shanghai as the No. 4-ranked women's strawweight, taking on No. 14 Denise Gomes in the co-main event.There is plenty around the fight for Yan to think about. She is 37, has been out of action since April 2025 and returns after a unanimous-decision loss to Virna Jandiroba. Before that, she had beaten Tabatha Ricci in 2024, following her five-round title fight against Zhang Weili at UFC 300. The division, meanwhile, has moved on in her absence, with Mackenzie Dern now holding the belt.Yan, though, is not interested in looking that far ahead. "I am not going to think about the championship right now. Right now, my priority is the first fight. I am going to pay attention to this fight and try to win this fight," she told the Times of India in an exclusive interaction.Yan keeps the title picture out of focusAnd the thought process extends to what comes after Gomes. Asked who would make sense as her next opponent if she wins, Yan did not name a contender. "I am open-minded. I am just waiting for whoever the next opponent is. I don't really care."It is a straightforward philosophy for a fighter whose position in the division makes Saturday important. Yan remains fourth in the UFC rankings, while Gomes is 14th and enters the fight on a four-fight winning streak.A long layoff, but a more experienced fighterFor Gomes, it is an opportunity to make a significant jump. For Yan, it is a chance to re-establish herself after the longest gap between UFC appearances of her career. She does not see the layoff as having left her the same fighter."I am definitely more experienced and more mature since last year. I have more experience, definitely."Yan points instead to the accumulated work - her skills, her strengths and the people around her."I am totally ready for the fight. Whatever skills I have improved, whatever strengths I have, and even the team - the whole team is from the US - have helped me. I am definitely more experienced, and the whole team has improved as well."Denise Gomes presents a very different testThe opponent, meanwhile, does not appear to have generated much anxiety. Gomes 26, has seven knockout wins and has won four consecutive UFC fights, most recently beating Tecia Pennington by unanimous decision in November.What does Yan see as the biggest threat?"There is no threat at all. I am just going to be myself, use whatever I have trained, and perform my game," she said.That confidence will be tested against a younger opponent who has steadily climbed the strawweight rankings. Gomes is fighting the biggest name of her UFC career, while Yan is fighting to keep herself in the part of the division where another title opportunity remains possible.But even the changing title picture - Dern's reign, Zhang Weili's move towards flyweight and Yan's No. 4 position - is not something she wants occupying her mind this week.Shanghai return brings excitement, not pressureThe setting, however, is different. Shanghai marks Yan's return to the city after nine years. UFC's August 29 event is its return to Shanghai, with Yan and Song Yadong giving the promotion two of China's biggest MMA names on the card. Song headlines against Umar Nurmagomedov, while Yan faces Gomes in the co-main event.There is no sense from Yan that the occasion has become a burden. "After nine years, I am returning to Shanghai for the UFC. There is no pressure at all. It is just more exciting, and I am more excited to fight."She will also have Song, her fellow Chinese UFC fighter and Team Alpha Male teammate, alongside her during fight week."We are from the same team, and it definitely improves my confidence. I am really happy to work together with Song Yadong, and hopefully we can both win our fights."Nine years after her last fight in Shanghai, Yan will walk into the Octagon again in her home country. articles.title: Tyson Fury fight with Anthony Joshua will go ahead in 2026 in America, predicts promoter Frank Warren
articles.summary: Talks are ongoing over a possible November blockbuster clash between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua; an apparent dispute over the location of the fight led to Fury claiming that the event was in "serious doubt"
articles.body:
Everything seemed to be in place for the British pair of former world champions to meet in London in November, but Saudi organisers Sela's desire to instead hold the event in the USA has created a hold up.

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has been pushing to keep the fight in London, which led to Fury claiming last week that the contest was in "serious doubt" because his rival was asking for "more money".

However, Fury's promoter Warren has allayed fears the fight could be called off, and insists The Gypsy King would also have preferred it to take place in the UK.

Warren told Sky Sports News : "I genuinely think it will happen. His Excellency, Turki Al-Alsheikh, he will announce that fairly soon.

"I know there's been some issues with contracts with Matchroom and AJ; I believe they will iron all those out.

"In the meantime, Tyson [Fury] has flown off to the States, he's in Miami and he's preparing for the fight.

"I think they both want the fight at Wembley, but it's out of their hands now. That's not quite right, actually, they could refuse to fight. We don't get the fight we want to see.

"I think because of the amount of money involved, I hope I'm wrong, but I think it will go on in America."

'Nothing unusual' for all-British clash to take place abroad

Warren says the fight taking place outside of the UK would be "nothing unusual" in terms of boxing's history.

"You had two massive American heroes in Muhammad Ali and George Foreman," Warren said. "Two American fighters, all the Americans wanted to see it, Vegas wanted to put the fight on, Madison Square Gardens wanted to see it, and it went off to Zaire.

"Everybody thought: 'What on earth was that all about?' But it became not just an iconic fight and an iconic moment in sport.

"Ali had the 'Thrilla in Manila' with Joe Frazier. Joe Bugner fought Ali in Kuala Lumpur, it's nothing unusual.

"I think it's like all sportsmen, say, for example, David Beckham, he went off and played at the end of his career [abroad], and he did that because of the money.

"And that's why these guys are doing this, they are professional boxers.

"Would I like to see it at Wembley? Would all the fans like to see it at Wembley? Of course they would. But they are in the hands of another broadcaster who wants the fight in America."

articles.title: Asian Games boxing selection twist: Sumit Kundu returns after Ministry intervention, Deepak Punia back in reserve
articles.summary: Boxing News: NEW DELHI: In yet another bizarre twist to Indiaâs Asian Games boxing selection, Sumit Kundu has retained his place in the menâs 70kg squad despite lo.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In yet another bizarre twist to Indiaâs Asian Games boxing selection, Sumit Kundu has retained his place in the menâs 70kg squad despite losing a fresh trial to Deepak Punia, who has now been relegated to reserve.The sports ministryâs final Indian contingent list has named Kundu in the 11-member boxing team â six men and five women â effectively overriding the outcome of the Boxing Federation of Indiaâs (BFI) closed-door trials at NIS Patiala on August 17.The development raises an obvious question: if Kundu was always going to remain the first-choice boxer, why was the fresh trial conducted in the first place?The BFI had originally finalised its Glasgow CWG and Aichi-Nagoya Asiad squads following trials at NIS Patiala on May 13-15. The decision to reopen three categories â menâs 70kg and 90kg, and womenâs 65kg â came after recommendations from the high-performance unit, support staff and selection committee.Kundu, who had been originally selected, lost to reserve Punia in the 70kg bout and was replaced. The trial minutes stated that the winner would be Rank 1 for the Asiad, while the loser would remain reserve. However, they also carried a caveat that if the ministry and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) did not accept the revised entries, the boxers who had represented India at the CWG would retain their Asiad berths.That is precisely what has happened. Kapil Pokhariya retained his 90kg place after beating Harsh Choudhary, while Parveen Hooda stayed in the womenâs 65kg category after defeating Saneh.BFI sources said the trials were necessitated to identify Indiaâs best medal prospects after the trio failed to win medals at the CWG. Kundu lost 1-4 to Northern Irelandâs Jon McConnell in the pre-quarters in Glasgow.But the process has left both Kundu and Punia paying the price. Sources said Sumit was around 75-76kg before the trial, making repeated weight cuts particularly demanding. After preparing for the CWG and August 17 trial, he must again cut weight for the Asiad, leaving his body completely drained.It has been learnt that the boxing contingent is scheduled to leave India on September 4 for a pre-Games training camp in Japan before travelling directly to the Games.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Makhachev habla de su futuro en la UFC: "Me esperan al menos tres combates más"
articles.standfirst: El peleador daguestaní quiere seguir defendiendo su cinturón de peso wélter hasta conseguir 20 victorias consecutivas en la compañía
articles.summary: El peleador daguestaní quiere seguir defendiendo su cinturón de peso wélter hasta conseguir 20 victorias consecutivas en la compañía
articles.body: El pasado 15 de agosto Islam Makhachev agrandó aún más su legado tras imponerse por decisión unánime a Ian Garry y defender por primera vez el cinturón de peso wélter. Tras batir el récord histórico de defensas en peso ligero y convertirse en doble campeón subiendo a 170 libras, el número uno del ránking libra por libra volvió a brillar para superar a Anderson Silva y quedarse líder en solitario como el peleador con más victorias consecutivas en la UFC -17-, aunque tiene pensado llegar a las 20. El peleador daguestaní sabe que el peso wélter es la categoría más competitiva de la UFC en la actualidad, por lo que quiere medirse a los nombres más importantes para demostrar que sigue vigente a sus 34 años y todavía tiene gasolina en el tanque. Es cierto que aún no ha conseguido finalizar a ningún oponente tras subir de división, pero su grappling de élite le ha bastado para dominar a dos oponentes duros como Ian Garry y Jack Della Maddalena. Tras su llegada a Daguestán, el mejor amigo de Khabib Nurmagomedov fue entrevistado por 'Ushatayka', afirmando que "no sé qué otros récords podré batir, pero ahora mismo en mi categoría hay algunos aspirantes al título muy fuertes. De cara al futuro, creo que me esperan al menos tres combates más". Todo hace indicar que su siguiente rival será Carlos Prates, que parece haber tomado la delantera a Michael Morales. El peleador brasileño de los 'Fighting Nerds' es el striker más temible de la división, aunque muchos dicen que Islam le prefiere porque será más fácil de derribar que Morales, Rakhmonov u otro tipo de peleador con mejor defensa de lucha que 'The Nightmare'. Makhachev ya ha afirmado que quiere volver antes del Ramadán del año que viene para no esperar tanto tiempo hasta su siguiente defensa, y ha sido Prates el que le ha retado para verse las caras en el Madison Square Garden de Nueva York en el UFC 334 de noviembre. Sin embargo, tres meses parecen muy pocos para que le dé tiempo al daguestaní a realizar un nuevo campamento y recuperarse de sus heridas en la cara. En ese mismo escenario fue donde hace un año Makhachev se convirtió en doble campeón tras dominar a Jack Della Maddalena, y donde Prates demostró que puede noquear a cualquiera tras ser el primero que lo hacía ante todo un ex campeón como Leon Edwards. De momento habrá que esperar, pero sus caminos parecen destinados a encontrarse más pronto que tarde, ya que ambos han dado luz verde para que suceda.

articles.title: Boxing: Moses Itauma says Filip Hrgovic's taunts are winding him up before world title fight
articles.summary: Moses Itauma says Filip Hrgovic's comments are starting to "wind him up" before their fight on Saturday.
articles.body:
Moses Itauma says Filip Hrgovic's comments are starting to "wind him up" before their IBF heavyweight world title fight on Saturday.

A victory at the O2 Arena would mean 21-year-old Itauma becomes the second youngest heavyweight world champion in history, behind only Mike Tyson.

The British fighter is the favouite going into the contest, but Hrgovic has been trying to taunt his rival by calling him a "kid" and "inexperienced".

"I tell myself there's nothing that this Hrgovic guy can do to get in my head but he's starting to wind me up," Itauma said.

"In an interview earlier, apparently he said I wake up and I just hug trees. He's really starting to annoy me.

"In my mind if somebody's trying to get one up on you, or trying to get in your head, it's because they're not confident in themselves. Obviously Hrgovic is a talker."

Croatia's Hrgovic, 13 years Itauma's senior, has suggested that victory for his opponent could have a negative affect on Itauma's future and that losing the fight would "save his soul".

"He's already in the clouds. He's already delusional," Hrgovic said.

"It can ruin your soul, it can make you lose yourself and we've seen a lot of superstars and famous people who have lost themselves.

"They're just lost in that crazy world of fame and money. He's not ready for that. I think, for him, it would be best to lose this fight, to save his soul.

"Because what does it mean to achieve everything if you lose your soul and you lose yourself?"

Itauma has had a fast rise to the peak of the boxing mountain, making his professional debut less than four years ago and having 14 fights in that time, knocking his opponent out in all but two of them.

"I wouldn't say he has a point but if I win this fight it might not be good for my soul," Itauma conceded.

"That's not the reason why I'm just gonna go in there and not win â for the sake of my soul. That's not a good idea."

articles.title: Islam Makhachev Reveals How Many UFC Fights He Has Left
articles.summary: UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev revealed how many fights he has left in his UFC career before he retires from MMA.At age 34, Makhachev is still in...
articles.body:
UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev revealed how many fights he has left in his UFC career before he retires from MMA.

At age 34, Makhachev is still in the prime of his athletic career. He is 29-1 in MMA, including an 18-1 record in the UFC, and recently set the longest win streak in promotional history with 17 straight victories.

He is a two-division UFC champion, and he is the No. 1 pound-for-pound fighter in the world right now. Having accomplished so much, there has been some chatter that Makhachev could walk away on top of his game, just like his friend and teammate Khabib Nurmagomedov did.

But Makhachev says he's not done just yet.

Islam Makhachev Says He Has 3 UFC Fights Left

Speaking to reporters in Dagestan after defeating Ian Machado Garry at UFC 330 , Makhachev revealed how many fights he has left in his UFC career, saying he has at least three more fights left in him against really tough opponents.

"Well, I wouldn't call (the win streak record) unbreakable by any means. There are fighters out there, not exactly breathing down my neck, but there are those that already have 10 wins (in a row). I don't know, maybe the title fights record? Though the record for title fights is quite large. I fought 10 bouts before getting the title, while the record holder fought for the title in his third or fourth fight. So I don't know what records will come next, but in my weight class I have some very good title contenders. I think I have at least three more spectacular and very tough fights for me," Makhachev said (via MMAFighting.com ).

After beating Makhachev at UFC 330, the Russian will likely fight Carlos Prates for his next fight, either later this year or early next year. Although the UFC hasn't announced anything yet, the smart money is on Prates getting the title shot.

Michael Morales is another top contender vying for the UFC welterweight title, and you can't completely forget about Shavkat Rakhmonov, the former No. 1 contender who hasn't fought in nearly two years due to injuries.

articles.title: Charles Oliveira Calls for UFC Rematch With Justin Gaethje
articles.summary: UFC BMF champion Charles Oliveira called for a rematch against Justin Gaethje, with both the BMF and lightweight titles on the line. Oliveira defeated Gaethj...
articles.body:
UFC BMF champion Charles Oliveira called for a rematch against Justin Gaethje, with both the BMF and lightweight titles on the line.

Oliveira defeated Gaethje in the main event of UFC 274 in May 2022 in a fight in which Oliveira, who was the UFC lightweight champion at the time, missed weight on the scale.

During the fight, Gaethje knocked the Brazilian down early on in the bout, but Oliveira regained his composure and was able to submit Gaethje soon thereafter after scoring. knockdown of his own.

Now, four years later, Oliveira is calling for the two to fight again, this time with Gaethje as the champion and Oliveira chasing his belt.

Charles Oliveira Wants Rematch With Justin Gaethje

Speaking to Brazilian MMA reporter Olhar da Luta, Oliveira made it clear that he wants Gaethje next with both the BMF and UFC lightweight titles on the line.

"With all due respect, I'm not looking backward. I'm looking forward. I want to fight for the title. That's what I'm focused on. The UFC likes a story… I was robbed (in our first fight). They wanted to distract me so I would go in there, have an (expletive) fight, and they could crown him champion. He felt my hands, I dropped him and then I submitted him. There's a story there. And now he's the champion. I have no problem with that. The rematch doesn't need to be in Brazil. Just like I went to his home turf before, it can be in his backyard, it can be in Las Vegas, on the street corner, in Japan, anywhere in the world. I just need one phone call telling me the date and time. So if the UFC wants a story, what bigger story is there than that?" Oliveira said.

While Oliveira vs. Gaethje is a fine rematch, it's hard to say that Oliveira deserves the title shot more than the winner of the UFC 331 co-main event between Arman Tsarukyan and Mauricio Ruffy, a fight that seems like a No. 1 contender bout.

Oliveira was actually slated to fight Tsarukyan originally on this card, but after his long-time teammate Allan Nascimento passed away, Oliveira was forced to withdraw from the bout, which is understandable.

We'll see what the UFC ultimately decides to do, but there is no doubt a rematch between Oliveira and Gaethje would be fun for the fans to watch.

In the "Featured" bout, Scottish killer Sean Clancy Jr. (8-0) fights former BKFC fighter, Gary Balletto (11-3). Welterweights hook 'em up as Ronald Humphrey (4-0) takes on Alexis Miranda (9-2). Finally, CFFC Welterweight champion, Nick Galanti (7-1), locks horns with Carlos Petruzzella (15-1).
